architecture.title: One workflow file, three front ends — NAT between you and the Spark's model
architecture.caption: configs/hotel_agent.yml names an OpenAI-compatible model server, three tools and an agent loop. NAT builds them and puts a front end in front: nat run (console), nat serve (REST + /v1/chat/completions on :8400) or nat mcp serve (the tools as MCP on :9901). The two hotel tools come from the hotel_ops_nat plugin package through the nat.components entry point. The model runs in vLLM on the Spark (or Ollama on the laptop as a labelled stand-in); NAT itself needs no GPU.

charts.title: Where one agent run spent its time (laptop stand-in)
charts.caption: From the trace timestamps of one lab 14-2 run on this Mac: nemotron-3-nano on a shared laptop Ollama — LAPTOP STAND-IN, not Spark numbers. The point is the shape: the tools take milliseconds, the model calls take the time. Faster serving (vLLM on the Spark, Modules 05–07) shortens the model bars; the agent code does not change.
